 Blue Raiders go for bowl eligibility at Sam Houston Saturday
 11/20/2026 12:00:00 PM | Football
 Share: Kickoff set for 1 PM on ESPN+
 By: @MTAthletics 
 Saturday, Nov. 21 | 1:02 p.m. | Bowers Stadium (14,500) | Huntsville, Tex. 
 MIDDLE TENNESSEE 
 BLUE RAIDERS 
 5-5, 3-3 CUSA 
 AT 
 SAM HOUSTON 
 BEARKATS 
 1-9, 0-6 CUSA 
 WATCH: ESPN+ | STATS: LINK | RADIO: WGNS ( LINK ) 
 GAME 11 
 » Saturday, Nov. 21 - 1:02 p.m. CT
» Bowers Stadium
» Huntsville, Tex.
 SERIES HISTORY 
 » This will be just the fifth all-time meeting in football between MTSU and Sam Houston and the third as conference foes. The series stands tied at 2-2 following the Blue Raiders' win last season. SHSU won the first meeting, 27-13, in the 1956 Refrigerator Bowl in Evansville, Ind. before the Blue Raiders took a 20-19 OT win at home during the 1991 I-AA Playoffs. Sam Houston won the 2023 meeting in Huntsville, 23-20 before MTSU took last year's game, 31-17, in Murfreesboro. 
 BLUE RAIDER NOTES 
 » MTSU is 5-2 all-time on Nov. 21 and has won five straight. Last loss on Nov. 21 came in 1981. 
 » A win over Sam Houston would make MTSU bowl eligible for the first time since 2022. 
 » Dominic Bourgeois ranks 23rd nationally in field goals made per game at 1.56 
 » QB Roman Gagliano has 18 TD passes this season which equals the ninth highest single-season total in MTSU history. Two more will tie him for eighth. 
 » Santana Fleming ranks 11th nationally and 1st in CUSA in kickoff return average at 24.9 
 » The Blue Raiders have lost just seven turnovers all season to rank 10th nationally and lead CUSA 
 » The 51 points scored against WKU is the most put up in the Derek Mason era. 
 » The Blue Raider offense has committed just seven turnovers in its last 12 games combined. 
 » MTSU's weather delay was 4:13 in win over Murray State and marked the third straight year the Blue Raiders have had a home game interrupted for weather. They had 2:40 delay in 2024 against TTU and a 2:12 delay against Marshall last year. That totals 9:05 in delays or right at 3 games. 
 » An emphasis for the Blue Raider offense in 2026 is to increase the amount of explosive plays (20 or more yards). In 2024 and 2025 combined, the offense had just 89 explosive plays with 45 coming last season. In 2026 they have 34 (8 vs Murray State, 5 vs FIU, 5 vs WKU). 
 » MTSU has six coaches who have either played or coached at the NFL level ( Derek Mason , Brian Stewart , Calvin Lowry , Louie Cioffi, and Josh Smith). 
 » Consecutive Starts: Korey Smith 14, Roman Gagliano 13 
» MTSU's last 1,000-yard rusher was Asher O'Hara in 2019 and he was a quarterback. The last running back to top 1,000 yards was I'Tavius Mathers in 2016.
» MTSU is one of just 12 schools in FBS to have a candidate on the Lou Groza and Ray Guy Watch Lists and the only Group of 6 team.
» The 2026 season for MTSU is the 112th for Blue Raider football and the 28th at the FBS level. 
 LACY EYEING TOP TEN 
 » WR Cam Lacy, who has at least one catch in 18 straight games,  is enjoying a career season as he is also embarking on entering the top 10 at MTSU for career receptions and yardage. The Toccoa, Ga., native has a personal-best 64 catches to rank 16th nationally with 6.4 receptions a contest to go with four touchdowns and 676 total yards (359 of those yards have been after the catch). Lacy, who has three career 100-yard receiving games, has 122 career receptions for 1,415 yards. Lacy needs two more catches to tie Jaylin Lane for 10th all-time and five to tie Ed Batties for ninth. He also needs 143 more yards to tie Vince Parks for 10th all-time.  
 SMITH IS A TACKLING MACHINE 
 » Linebacker Korey Smith , who starred at Murfreesboro's Oakland High School, enters the Sam Houston game leading the team in total tackles with 96 after having double digit stops in six of his last nine games. His 9.6 stops per game currently ranks second-most in Conference USA and 13th in the nation. SMThe junior turned in his career-high in tackles with 16 on the road against Liberty. In 28 years competing at the FBS level, MTSU has had 11 100 tackles or more seasons (and only four linebackers) and Smith is on pace to be No. 12. He also needs 23 more stops to tie T.T. Barber for 10th on the all-time single-season list. 
 BOURGEOIS CHASING RECORD 
 »  Dominic Bourgeois has connected on 13 of 16 three-pointers this season. The all-time single-season record is 18 set by Crews Holt (2018) and Alan Gendreau (2009). The 13 made field goals are the most by an MTSU kicker since Zeke Rankin hit 16 in 2022. He needs one more to equal the eighth most in a single-season. 
 GAGLIANO HAS IMPRESSIVE STARTER NUMBERS 
 » Signal-caller Roman Gagliano has made 13 career starts with three to end the 2025 season and the 10 games this year. In those 13 starts, the Opelika, AL, native has accounted for 3,438 yards of total offense with 3,012 passing yards, 426 rushing yards and been responsible for 29 touchdowns. More importantly is the fact he has thrown 477 career passes with 25 touchdowns and only four interceptions. His 6.25 TD to INT ratio ranks 4th best among active players in the FBS. 
 OFFENSIVE EXPLOSION BREAKS DROUGHT 
 » MTSU ended a seven-year drought against WKU in large part due to an impressive offensive output. The Blue Raiders put up 51 points, 513 yards and no turnovers in the win. It was the most points scored in the Derek Mason era and the most by the Blue Raiders since scoring 51 points in a win over Old Dominion in 2018. The 513 yards marked the first time the unit has topped the 500 mark since gaining 541 yards at WKU in 2025. It was also the fifth time this season MTSU has not committed a turnover.  
 MARTIN COMING UP BIG IN RUN GAME 
 » After a career-best day against WKU, running back Antonio Martin Jr. now has five 100-yard rushing games on the year. He is the first Blue Raider to have five 100-yard games in a season since I'Tavius Mathers in 2016 (Mathers had 8). Martin, who had 125 yards and a personal-best two TDs in the win over WKU, has had 100 yard games against Murray State, Nevada, Jax State, and KSU. Entering the Sam Houston game, Martin has 750 rushing yards.  
 CHASING 1,000 
 » Antonio Martin has his sights set on becoming the 12th different player in MTSU history to reach the 1,000-yard mark and the first since 2019 when quarterback Asher O'Hara had 1,058 yards. The last MTSU running back to record 1,000 yards in a season was I'Tavius Mathers in 2016 when he had 1,561 yards. Martin enters play against Sam Houston with 750 yards and the possibility of three more games puts him well in reach.
